I always carry a small folding knife.

I used to drive a horse drawn carriage up on Mackinac Island giving tours during the summer. One day during a tour I noticed a commotion at the top of a hill during one of my tours and drove over to see what was up. One of the dray drivers had pushed his team of horses up the hill. A dray is like the cargo truck of horse drawn wagons, usually just a flat bead trailer. One of the horses had collapsed and was badly tangled in its harness, I noticed in particular that the line (thats the part that attaches to the bit in the horses mouth) had some how gotten around its neck and that the quarter strap was wrapped around the horses leg.

The horse was freaking out, obviously, and the dray driver must have been really green because he was like a deer in the headlights. I ended up asking a tourist to hold my horses (they were a good team and knew not to move until I told them to so it was safe, I promise) while I jumped down to help the fallen horse out.

I ended up sitting on the horses neck/shoulder to make sure he wasn't moving his head too much and that calmed him down a lot. The first thing I did was use my trusty knife to cut the line that was wrapped around his neck and the I cut through the harness right behind the collar. Basically, with two easy cuts I had completely destroyed the harness so as I stood up I just pulled it off with me. By this time the guys from the barns had gotten word what was going on and showed up to help. My knife saved a life and now I almost always keep it with me.

Another good story was from last month when I had to pull my knife out to get a homeless man to leave my girlfriend alone...
I always carry a knife and once used it to free a turtle that was tangled in carelessly discarded fishing line.
A life is a life even if there's no tourists around to pat your back afterward.
